approach: Acceleration equals velocity times the rate of change of velocity with displacement, a = v(dv/ds).

steps.text: Write acceleration using the chain rule for motion described by velocity as a function of displacement.
The velocity decreases at 3 m/s for every metre of displacement, so dv/ds is negative.
Substitute v = 10 m/s and dv/ds = −3 (m/s)/m into a = v(dv/ds) to get the acceleration.
steps.why_this_step: a = v dv/ds is the standard way to find acceleration when velocity is given as a function of position, not time.

common_mistakes.text: Dropping the negative sign on the rate of decrease and writing a = 10 × 3 = 30 m/s².
Writing a = dv/ds = −3 m/s² directly, leaving out the factor of v from the chain rule.
